title: Mick Woodmansey - Wikipedia
notes: Michael 'Woody' Woodmansey, born 4 February 1950, Driffield, East Riding of Yorkshire. Joined Bowie's band Hype at Mick Ronson's suggestion in late March 1970, replacing John Cambridge; lived at Haddon Hall with Bowie, Ronson and Visconti; recorded The Man Who Sold the World, then with Ronson and Trevor Bolder as the Spiders from Mars Hunky Dory (1971), Ziggy Stardust (1972) and Aladdin Sane (1973), and the Ziggy Stardust tour. Dismissed in July 1973 and replaced by Aynsley Dunbar (Pin Ups). Bowie, 1994: 'He was quite open to direction and in a way sort of carried out what I wanted done much more than most of the other drummers I have worked with.' Later: the Spiders from Mars album (1976), U-Boat (1977), Screen Idols, Art Garfunkel, Holy Holy with Visconti (from 2014). Memoir Spider From Mars: My Life With David Bowie (2016, with Joel McIver).

title: Jamming Good: Spiders Drummer Woody Woodmansey's Favourite Bowie Moments (the Quietus, Baker's Dozen)
notes: 22 February 2017, thirteen songs in his own words. Five Years: 'that beat came out of sort of despair and apathy'. Moonage Daydream: 'you had to keep grounded, keep that solid beat going and not be affected'. Rock 'n' Roll Suicide: 'There are times when it breaks down to just the bass drum, and that bass drum needs to be played with despair.' Life on Mars?: 'I went through the string arrangement and knew what I could and couldn't do ... It still needed to be a solid beat, but kind of a futuristic-meets-classic rock thing'; three takes, the phone ringing over the third. Changes: 'For me as a drummer I went for less-is-more ... I even tried putting little drum rolls on it here and there ... It sounded like being flashy for the sake of it.' Ziggy Stardust: 'I was really into King Crimson at the time and I loved the drummer. He used to play things, strange drum rolls at strange places in the song ... I definitely took a bit of inspiration from King Crimson for my playing on that one.' The Jean Genie: 'that one was a first take – that's what's on the record.'

title: Woody Woodmansey on David Bowie (the Strange Brew, Jason Barnard)
notes: 'John Bonham from Zeppelin was a big hero of mine'; listening to 'anything from Cream to Zeppelin, Hendrix, Jeff Beck Group and the blues', later Neil Young and Crazy Horse and Lennon. On Hunky Dory: 'you could put a song across really well without doing licks at 1000 miles an hour ... don't play if it's not going to really add, leave it and then make an entrance when it needs it.' On The Man Who Sold the World: Visconti 'introduced me to timpani and wood blocks and maracas ... I'd never really played all that stuff'; 'We always looked at it, as our Sgt Pepper.'

title: Suffragette City - the Bowie Bible
notes: Recorded 4 February 1972; Bowie, Ronson, Bolder, Woodmansey; quotes his book: 'when I tried different beats the song was diminished ... the beat that is on there keeps the listener involved and doesn't let up.'

title: David Bowie - Starman (Live on Top of the Pops, 1972) [Official Video]
notes: BBC One, 6 July 1972 (recorded 5 July, mimed to a backing track of 29 June). Woodmansey at the back: a rose-pink satin jumpsuit, light brown hair in a feathered shag to the collar with long sideburns, clean-shaven; a bass drum in a grey marbled pearl wrap, chrome, brass cymbals. Watched as contact sheets.

title: Ziggy Stardust (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at Trident on 11 November 1971, co-produced by Ken Scott; Ronson, Bolder, Woodmansey.

title: Suffragette City - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at Trident on 4 February 1972 with Starman and Rock n Roll Suicide; offered first to Mott the Hoople.

title: Moonage Daydream - Wikipedia
notes: The Arnold Corns single (February 1971, drummer Tim Broadbent); re-recorded with the Spiders at Trident on 12 November 1971.

title: Starman (David Bowie song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at Trident on 4 February 1972; Top of the Pops recorded 5 July, broadcast 6 July 1972, mimed to a backing track recorded 29 June.

title: Life on Mars? - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at Trident on 6 August 1971, the last day of the Hunky Dory sessions; Wakeman piano, Ronson's strings. In Spider from Mars (2016) Woodmansey called it the highlight of his recording career with Bowie, the track he is 'most proud of'.

title: Changes (David Bowie song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at Trident on 30 July 1971; mostly 4/4, two bars of 2/4 and four of 3/4 'accompanied by Woodmansey's drum fills'; piano and kick drum eighths build into the chorus.

title: The Jean Genie - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at RCA Studios, New York, 6 October 1972, co-produced by Ken Scott; the Spiders.

title: The Man Who Sold the World (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Backing track recorded at Trident on 4 May 1970, produced by Tony Visconti (bass); Woodmansey drums and percussion; Ralph Mace Moog; vocals at Advision on 22 May.

title: Hunky Dory - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded mid-1971 at Trident with Ronson, Bolder and Woodmansey, co-produced by Ken Scott; Woodmansey and Ronson had left in August 1970 and were brought back.

title: Aladdin Sane - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded December 1972 to January 1973 between tour legs, at Trident and RCA New York; the last album with the full Spiders line-up; The Jean Genie the first song recorded.
